trust_decision.summary: Whether a request may carry a sensitive header is decided per request in Mechanize::HTTP::Agent#request_add_headers by drop_after_redirect?(name, crossed_origin), but crossed_origin describes only the immediately preceding hop and is absent (defaults false) on the auth-retry and robots.txt fetches, so the credential decision is re-derived per call instead of being a property of the operation.

landing_point.why: The summary is 'credential headers to another host after an HTTP redirect'; response_redirect is where the Location is resolved, where the header hash is filtered for the next hop, and where crossed_origin is computed.

fix_sites.entry_point: Mechanize::HTTP::Agent#fetch (reachable directly via Mechanize#agent, lib/mechanize.rb:1274) and the Mechanize#get/verb family at lib/mechanize.rb:483
request_add_headers, the single sink every request passes through
Mechanize#get on a 3xx with redirect_ok set (default true)
Mechanize#get with follow_meta_refresh = true on a meta/Refresh redirect
Mechanize#get on a 401 where the auth store has credentials
Mechanize#get with robots = true (robots.txt lookup through webrobots)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The robots.txt lookup is a separate, opt-in subsystem (only when #robots = true, driven by the webrobots gem) that is not a redirect at all, so a solver can leave it to webrobots and still claim the advisory is fixed.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: A same-origin redirect or same-origin meta refresh must still send the agent's credential headers, and non-sensitive agent headers (X-Api-Key) must still follow a cross-origin redirect; an unconditional delete of @request_headers, or of the whole forwarded hash, breaks both.

O6_input_shapes: credential carried as an agent-level default (Mechanize#request_headers=) versus in the per-request headers hash
header-name spelling and case variants (AUTHORIZATION, cookie, Proxy-Authorization, Cookie2) matched with casecmp?
sensitive and non-sensitive headers sharing the one merged hash that is carried between hops

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second internal auxiliary fetch that reuses #fetch (a sitemap, favicon or robots-adjacent lookup) and therefore re-applies the caller's headers.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: get_robots already does exactly this: it wraps #fetch inside the Robots section, so a maintainer adding another auxiliary request would copy that shape.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Page::Image#fetch resolves an on a foreign host and calls mech.get, which applies @request_headers to that host.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The feature already routes through the agent with a page referer, so making it origin-aware is a one-line change a maintainer could plausibly write in the same fix.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A per-verb helper (request_with_entity) that re-enters agent.fetch with current_page as referer and no origin state.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The put/post helpers already call agent.fetch directly, so any new verb helper or retry wrapper lands on the same sink.

O10_build.toolchain: Ruby >= 2.6, bundler + rake; gemspec runtime deps addressable, domain_name, http-cookie, mime-types, net-http-digest_auth, net-http-persistent, nokogiri, webrick, webrobots, rubyntlm, base64, nkf; Gemfile adds minitest, rake, rdoc, rubocop, brotli, zstd-ruby
O10_build.project_tests: Minitest: test/test_mechanize_http_agent.rb (agent behaviour, redirects, meta refresh, auth, robots) plus test/test_mechanize.rb; the harness stubs Net::HTTP#request in-process at lib/mechanize/test_case.rb:192-229 and serves /redirect, /http_refresh, /http_headers and /robots.txt from servlets, recording each request in Mechanize::TestCase::REQUESTS (lib/mechanize/test_case.rb:225), so no sockets or network are used.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Thread a sticky cross-origin flag through response_redirect so a second hop stays stripped - that keeps the one-hop tests green and leaves the 401 retry, the second meta refresh and the robots.txt fetch re-applying @request_headers.

out_of_scope_notes: Page::Image#fetch (lib/mechanize/page/image.rb:83-84) and Page::Link clicks send @request_headers to whatever host the href/src names; that is a fresh caller-requested fetch, not a redirect, so it falls outside this advisory's property and was not pursued.
